_comment: Source-of-truth variant + overlay table for the 18 research-foundry colonies. Phase 9 PR-B of #663 introduces this file so tools/cull-replicas.sh and the run-research.sh bootstrap loop can seed per-colony specialty pools without hardcoded tables. PR-C will use the same overlays for replica spawn loops in non-explorer colonies. Overlay texts for non-explorer colonies are 1-line stubs at PR-B; PR-C will refine them as it lights up per-role replication.

overlays.group_theory: Focus on finite group invariants: conjugacy classes, character tables, subgroup lattices, automorphism groups. Compute representations and quotients explicitly. Look for coincidences in character degrees, order divisibility, sporadic-vs-classical group behaviour.
overlays.combinatorics: Focus on enumerative combinatorics: generating functions, bijective proofs, lattice paths, partition identities. Compute small-case counts and look for OEIS matches. Compare known sequences against derived ones for unexpected coincidence.
overlays.number_theory: Focus on arithmetic functions and sieves: prime counting, Mobius, totient, divisor sums. Compute over small ranges, examine mod-p behaviour, look for unexpected density / equidistribution / sign-change patterns.
overlays.probability: Focus on random structures: Erdos-Renyi graphs, random matrices, percolation thresholds, asymptotic distributions. Run small Monte Carlo and compare against predicted limits. Look for deviations from the expected scaling.
overlays.algebra: Focus on representation theory + Lie algebras: irreducible representations, weight diagrams, Casimir invariants, Cartan classification. Compute decomposition of tensor products, dimensions, branching rules. Look for unexpected multiplicities or symmetries.

overlays.subtle: Bias toward subtle surprises: small deviations from expected, off-by-one mismatches, low-magnitude regularities that classical results do not predict.
overlays.dramatic: Bias toward dramatic surprises: large numerical anomalies, order-of-magnitude collapses, qualitative regime changes.
overlays.coincidence: Bias toward coincidence surprises: two quantities computed via independent paths agreeing far more than chance would predict.
overlays.pattern: Bias toward pattern surprises: structural repetitions, fixed sub-sequences, modular regularities, recursive nesting.
overlays.symmetry: Bias toward symmetry surprises: unexpected group actions, hidden involutions, dual descriptions of the same object.

overlays.strict: Dismiss any surprise that can be plausibly explained by a single classical result; require clear novelty before passing through.
overlays.lenient: Pass surprises through unless they are clearly explained by a textbook identity; favour false positives over false negatives.
overlays.evidence: Anchor dismissals on cited evidence: require a specific theorem / identity / lemma reference before dismissing.
overlays.classical: Anchor dismissals on classical-mathematics base rates: dismiss surprises consistent with well-known asymptotics.
overlays.compute: Anchor dismissals on compute-time check: dismiss only when a quick re-computation reproduces the predicted classical value.

overlays.terse: Formulate claims in terse mathematical prose: minimal words, maximal symbols, no narrative.
overlays.expansive: Formulate claims with full narrative motivation: explain why the surprise matters, what classical result it deviates from, what corollaries it suggests.
overlays.rigorous: Formulate claims in strict theorem/proof shape: hypothesis, claim, sketch of supporting evidence, explicit quantifiers.
overlays.operational: Formulate claims as operational recipes: how to reproduce the surprise from raw data, what input range matters, what observable to read.
overlays.historical: Formulate claims with historical anchoring: which classical theorem the surprise complements / refines, who originally posed the related question.

overlays.lightweight: Verify the claim only on the original sample input: cheap re-computation, no exploration of neighbouring inputs.
overlays.exhaustive: Verify the claim across the full feasible parameter range: scan every input the budget allows.
overlays.edge_case: Verify the claim with adversarial edge cases: boundary inputs, degenerate cases, known counter-example shapes.
overlays.small_n: Verify the claim by brute-forcing the smallest n values: hand-checkable computation for sanity.
overlays.asymptotic: Verify the claim by extrapolating to large n: confirm the regularity persists past the bootstrap sample range.

overlays.strict: Set the NOVEL bar high: only claims with no plausible classical counterpart pass through.
overlays.lenient: Set the NOVEL bar low: anything beyond direct restatement of a known identity is a candidate.
overlays.literature: Anchor novelty on literature absence: a claim is NOVEL only if no paper / textbook excerpt found matches it.
overlays.construct: Anchor novelty on the construction: same identity expressed in a new form / domain still counts as NOVEL.
overlays.domain: Anchor novelty on cross-domain transfer: identities re-derivable in a different mathematical area still count as NOVEL.

overlays.narrow: Query arXiv with narrow exact-phrase searches: prefer precision over recall.
overlays.broad: Query arXiv with broad keyword unions: prefer recall over precision; deduplicate downstream.
overlays.recent: Restrict arXiv queries to recent submissions (last 5 years) when scoring overlap with claim.
overlays.classical: Restrict arXiv queries to classical references (>10 years old) when scoring overlap with claim.
overlays.cross_field: Query arXiv across adjacent fields (e.g. math.CO and math.NT both for combinatorial number theory claims).

overlays.exact: Match OEIS sequences only on full prefix equality of the first N terms.
overlays.prefix: Match OEIS sequences on the longest common prefix shared with the claim's terms.
overlays.shifted: Match OEIS sequences allowing for index shifts (a(n+k) vs a(n)) before scoring overlap.
overlays.transformed: Match OEIS sequences after applying common transforms (differences, partial sums, ratios).
overlays.partial: Match OEIS sequences on partial sub-sequences appearing inside the candidate sequence.

overlays.surface: Match groupprops pages only on the landing-page summary: name, order, classification.
overlays.deep: Match groupprops pages after walking subgroup-lattice and quotient pages for related coincidences.
overlays.subgroup: Focus the groupprops lookup on the subgroup-lattice page for each candidate group.
overlays.automorphism: Focus the groupprops lookup on the automorphism-group page for each candidate group.
overlays.representation: Focus the groupprops lookup on the linear-representation page for each candidate group.

overlays.recent: Restrict Scholar queries to articles published in the last 5 years.
overlays.classical: Restrict Scholar queries to articles published >10 years ago, weight by citation count.
overlays.cited_by: Walk Scholar `cited-by` graphs outward from the top-1 hit before scoring overlap.
overlays.review: Prefer Scholar review / survey articles when scoring overlap with claim.
overlays.preprint: Prefer Scholar preprints (arXiv mirror, SSRN, bioRxiv math feeds) over journal articles.

overlays.consensus: Weight searcher / prior_advocate reports by how many of them agree; majority drives the verdict.
overlays.outlier: Weight searcher / prior_advocate reports by which one disagrees with the rest; outlier drives the verdict when its evidence is strong.
overlays.weighted: Weight each searcher's report by its declared confidence before summing into the verdict.
overlays.skeptical: Bias toward NOT_NOVEL: require strong, multi-source evidence to vote NOVEL.
overlays.advocate: Bias toward NOVEL: require a single source of strong prior evidence to vote NOT_NOVEL.

overlays.textbook: Cite the closest textbook chapter / exercise as prior evidence for the claim.
overlays.research_paper: Cite the closest peer-reviewed research paper as prior evidence for the claim.
overlays.lecture_notes: Cite the closest publicly-archived lecture notes / course handout as prior evidence.
overlays.qa_thread: Cite the closest mathoverflow / stackexchange thread as prior evidence.
overlays.blog: Cite the closest expert blog post / personal page as prior evidence.

overlays.specialist: Write the introduction for a specialist audience inside the claim's subfield: minimal background, dense notation.
overlays.broad_math: Write the introduction for a broad-math audience: bridge from related subfields, define every term used.
overlays.applied: Write the introduction for an applied-math audience: motivate via downstream applications of the claim.
overlays.undergrad: Write the introduction for a strong-undergraduate audience: friendly motivation, explicit examples before the abstract statement.
overlays.popularizer: Write the introduction for an interested-non-specialist audience: history, intuition, why the claim is surprising.

overlays.constructive: Prefer constructive proofs: build the witnessing object explicitly, avoid choice / contradiction.
overlays.non_constructive: Allow non-constructive proofs: extremal principles, fixed-point arguments, contradiction allowed.
overlays.computational: Prefer computational proofs: reduce the claim to a finite check the computer colony can run.
overlays.structural: Prefer structural proofs: lean on algebraic / categorical decompositions over case analysis.
overlays.asymptotic: Prefer asymptotic proofs: derive the claim from limit statements; finitary cases follow as corollaries.

overlays.sympy: Run the reproducibility check using sympy (symbolic). Cite the script verbatim in the appendix.
overlays.numpy: Run the reproducibility check using numpy (numerical). Report both float and rationalised values.
overlays.gap: Run the reproducibility check using GAP (group theory). Cite the script verbatim in the appendix.
overlays.sage_like: Run the reproducibility check using a sage-like superset (sympy + networkx + custom). Cite the script verbatim.
overlays.bruteforce: Run the reproducibility check via direct enumeration in pure Python. Cite the script verbatim.

overlays.copyedit: Focus editorial passes on copyediting: grammar, consistency, terminology unification.
overlays.typesetting: Focus editorial passes on typesetting: equation labels, cross-references, figure placement, latexmk hygiene.
overlays.structural: Focus editorial passes on structural rewrites: reorder sections, collapse redundant remarks, sharpen the abstract.
overlays.citation_audit: Focus editorial passes on citation audit: every numerical claim cites its searcher report, every cite verified.
overlays.abstract_polish: Focus editorial passes on abstract / first-paragraph polish: the part most readers actually read.

overlays.strict: Set the approval bar high: every numerical claim in the .tex must have direct support in the reproducibility output.
overlays.lenient: Set the approval bar lower: allow numerical claims supported only by adjacent computer-output values when the gap is explained.
overlays.claim_centric: Anchor the verdict on the claim list: enumerate, flag, approve only when every claim is supported.
overlays.evidence_centric: Anchor the verdict on the reproducibility output: every produced value must appear (or be derivable) somewhere in the .tex.
overlays.structural: Anchor the verdict on structural completeness: introduction / theorem / proof / reproducibility / references all present.

overlays.staged: Stage the arxiv-metadata.json + submission.tar.gz for HITL review before requesting SMTP send.
overlays.fast_track: Stage the submission and immediately request HITL review; surface the package on the dashboard.
overlays.hold: Stage the submission but defer the HITL ping until the operator explicitly toggles the colony.
overlays.metadata_first: Stage arxiv-metadata.json first and request HITL review of metadata before assembling submission.tar.gz.
overlays.validate_only: Stage the submission package and run validation passes (latexmk dry, sanity grep on .tex) before HITL ping.
